steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x9-inch baking pan.
Whisk flour, sugar, 2 tablespoon cocoa powder, baking powder, and salt together in a large bowl. Stir in milk and butter until smooth. Fold in walnuts until just combined.
Spread batter evenly into the prepared baking pan.
Combine brown sugar and ¼ cup cocoa powder in a small bowl; sprinkle on top of batter. Pour hot water over batter.

Bake in the preheated oven until center of cake is almost set, about 45 minutes. (Brown sugar, cocoa powder, and hot water will combine to form a chocolate sauce that will settle to the bottom of the cake during baking.) Serve it warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Hot Fudge Pudding Cake
raw_recipe.description: This hot fudge pudding cake recipe yields a rich, chocolatey cake that sits on a gooey hot fudge sauce. Serve it warm with whipped cream or ice cream.
raw_recipe.name: Hot Fudge Pudding Cake

review.reviewBody: This recipe is great. But, we always make sure we eat it right after it comes out of the oven. It isn't as good the next day. But, we usually don't have any left. Ooeeyyyyy Gooery!

This looks incredible when it’s taken from the oven. The dessert is all “chocolately” with the fudge sauce bubbling enticingly through the cake layer. I admit I’m a chocoholic and couldn’t wait to dig in. I made a mistake when I made the cake base using ¼ cup of cocoa instead of the two tablespoons. It must have been a Freudian slip. I also added ½ teaspoon of vanilla to the cake base and boiled the water before pouring it on the cake. I’ve made several pudding cakes but I like this one the best. There is plenty of chocolate sauce and it has great chocolate flavor. This was a last minute thought to make for dessert and had I planned to make this earlier I would have saved leftover coffee to add to the liquid to enhance the chocolate flavor. Serve warm with vanilla ice cream for a perfect dessert.

This chocoholic has been making this for 30 years:
1) Follow the liquid instructions exactly! Ignore all reviews that didn't do this.
2) Feel free to add a teaspoon of vanilla to cake batter.
3) Use boiling strong coffee instead of water, coffee always enhances chocolate flavor. I usually add instant coffee to the water.
4) Use good cocoa. Ignore any review saying it wasn't chocolately enough or too sweet, they aren't using good cocoa. I use Hershey's Special Dark (or Droste), it is like the difference between dollar store chocolate and Ghirardelli.
5) Eat warm with ice cream, it is not as good reheated.

I made this cake for my grand young 'uns and they loved it. I liked it too, but it was too "tame" for my wild & overactive taste buds.
I'm an old-fashioned, country cookin', 67 yr old grandma who loves highly seasoned food.
I tried this recipe because it is so similar to mine. 
In my recipe, I add 1 teaspoon vanilla to the batter; 2 teaspoons cornstarch and 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon to the dry cocoa/brown sugar; equal parts hot water and hot milk.
The cake is more flavorful and the sauce is creamier. 
(I use brown sugar in ALL chocolate batter.)
Sometimes I would add a bit of flavor to the hot milk/water and lightly dust the top of the baked cake with powdered sugar.
I've also made this cake by combining all the
dry ingredients for the sauce/pudding, add the hot milk/hot water, mix well, pour over the batter.
It worked for me! Deeeeelicious!!
Delicious and easy to make. So good with vanilla ice cream. Instead of baking in the oven, we cook it in microwave on High for 7 minutes in a glass mixing bowl. Love it!!!

It tasted good, but I believe the amount of hot water to pour over batter is too much. My pudding was runny. I couldn't find my regular recipe for this cake, so I used this one. I think everything is the same except for the amount of how water. I would say no more than 1/2 cup.

Oh my word! Excellent! I did double it since I knew we'd want leftovers so I baked it about 10 min longer. Also subbed boiling leftover coffee for the water as I have done in the past for similar recipes. A new favorite!! And it was just as good the next day, zapped in microwave with a scoop of vanilla ice cream on top!

My family loved it. Turned out really well and it was my first time baking such a cake. Followed the recipe as it. Had some trouble with the tablespoon of butter so I put the first mixture in the microwave for 15 sec. then the egg yolk mixture mixed perfectly with no pieces. Next time, I will melt/soften the butter first. The top wasn’t as brown after the 45 min so I monitored it for another 8 min until it turned brown and removed from the oven.

Originally I found this recipe in an old Hershey’s chocolate cookbook. I can make it vegan by using two tablespoons of canola oil instead of butter. Its easy to microwave the next day to enjoy it warm again.

The only change I made was to not add the nuts as the person for whom I was making it did not want the nuts added. This tastes like an old recipe that was in a Betty Crocker cookbook that I got as a wedding gift from my grandmother 53 years ago! Loved it and will make again and again!

I was trying to find a pudding cake recipe like the boxed mix they used to sell in my youth. This one seemed easy enough. Unfortunately, I also found this a bit watery and sickeningly sweet. Like another reviewer; I, too, reduced the sugar (1/2 cup in the cake, 2/3 cup in the sauce) and added about a tsp of vanilla to the cake. I also needed to add an extra 1/4 cup of milk to the cake, as the batter was literally like biscuit dough without it.

I used slivered almonds instead of walnuts in the cake. It added a nice texture.

Next time I'd suggest upping the butter to 1/4 cup, and/or using whole milk or light cream in both parts of the cake.

I've made this many times since I learned it in Girl Scouts, and I couldn't find my recipe but this one sounded really close to what I remembered. I had to bake this another 6 minutes as the cake was really jiggly and nowhere close to being what I'd call "almost set". It started getting dark though, so I pulled it and called it good enough. This is missing something, maybe a lot more cocoa? It was sweet and indeed had that pudding layer beneath it, but it was loose so I'd call it more of a sauce. Even once it cooled it wasn't as set as pudding is. It may be because I didn't use the walnuts and needed more flour to compensate. I am not sure what went wrong with this one. It wasn't as chocolatey as I expected, and didn't have the depth and richness of a chocolate brownie or layer cake. This reminded me of the flavor of a chocolate Texas sheet cake, a lot of sugar, a little chocolate, and mild in flavor. We weren't fans of this version. It is fun though to see it go in to the oven with all the water on top and then have it reverse and make a cake layer on top and a sauce layer on bottom just like magic.
Classic recipe my father taught me 35-40 years ago!! My sons favorite for their birthdays!! : )

I haven't made this for several years because I lost my recipe (or someone "borrowed" it because it was so popular!). I am thrilled to find this posted. It is exactly the way I've always made it. Don't change ANYTHING about it. It's easy and perfect just as it is written.

This has been in our family for 75 years or more, but I have been unable to find my stained recipe card with the words written on it. This looks close enough for me to give it a whirl. We just called it "Chocolate Pudding Cake".

I followed the recipe as written, and I wouldn't change a thing! The hot fudge pudding cake is everything you could want--it's not overly sweet, it's incredibly chocolatey, and it's oh-so-gooey! Serving it with a scoop of ice cream sends it to over-the-top magical levels! Thank you for sharing your recipe--this was super easy, and super delicious!!
Didn't need any changes. My husband is in chocolate heaven. It's definitely a keeper.
Easy peasy and delicious. No eggs a plus.

My mom always fixed this cake for us growing up. I double the recipe. We used regular granulated sugar in the topping instead of the brown sugar. It makes up very good and is very popular at church dinners, etc.
We love it. I've also made it with chocolate milk instead of milk and coffee instead of hot water. Both are deliscious.
